body.estimand_functional: \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)=\sup_{D_H(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\le\varepsilon}d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widetilde\theta)\), with the proved bound \(\Omega_{k,m}(\varepsilon)\ge c\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) on every class containing the lower family and the proved identity \(\Omega_{k,m}^{\mathrm{rad}}(\varepsilon)\asymp\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\); the matching full-class upper bound is the open question \(\mathrm{oeq:full\text{-}incompressible\text{-}rigidity}\).

sampling_model.design: One observational environment and two grouped positive stochastic perfect-intervention environments for every latent node; group labels are observed up to one common node permutation.
sampling_model.units: \(N\) independent observations from each environment on \(\mathbb T^n\), independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: The environment replaces exactly one latent conditional mechanism by a parent-free circular density \(q_i^e\) normalized with respect to \(d\lambda(t)=dt/(2\pi)\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every complete latent law is bounded between \(c_0\) and \(C_0\), and the decoder is uniformly bi-Lipschitz.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Positive truncated Fourier density estimation normalized by a convex floor construction that remains at least \(c_0/(2K^n)\), followed by a certified rational wrapped-spline minimum-distance fit; no derivative of an estimated density is required for the population residual reduction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Then CauCA in \((G,\mathcal F,\mathcal P_G)\) is identifiable up to \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{scaling}}\).
Two hard interventions with interventional discrepancy on the same target node suffice to recover that node up to a diffeomorphism.
Then there is \(A\in SO(d)\) such that \(g^{-1}\circ f(s)=As+h(s)+b\).
Algorithms 2 and 3 are consistent estimators of the latent graph and inverse transformation up to the corresponding equivalence classes.
With a large enough \(N\), the estimated cross-derivative vectors are almost zero for all coordinate pairs.

body.tldr: Complete paired interventions reveal a synthetic product law that controls decoder volume distortion for every DAG. Encoder error is measured by a symmetric quotient pseudometric: one common permutation and coordinatewise circle alignment is evaluated in both directed \(L^2\) losses and their maximum is minimized. The primary \(n=2\), \(C^2\) nondegenerate Morse class is defined directly by separated critical points and a nonzero one-dimensional Hessian, without importing a higher-smoothness quantitative-Morse theorem. A distinct novel finite-type rate class covers \(1\le m\le k-1\) with uniform margins, separation, and attained order, and an explicit periodic mechanism family and nonlinear torus shear certify nonemptiness of the strengthened density, \(C^k\), and bi-Lipschitz envelopes. The explicit Hamiltonian cylinder gives the \(3/4\) Morse lower order and the matching radial frontier. The open contribution remains arbitrary-map incompressible rigidity; an affirmative result yields the full \(\varepsilon^{(k+1)/(k+m+1)}\) modulus, the Fourier estimator clipped at \(c_0/(2K^n)\), and symmetric-quotient confidence sets.

project_justification.gap: CauCA and score-based causal representation learning establish componentwise exact identification under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy, but they do not metrize approximate recovery symmetrically or quantify isolated critical zeros. Quantitative Morse perturbation results requiring higher smoothness do not justify the primary \(C^2\) case, and near-isometry robustness controls a different primitive defect.
project_justification.niche: Circular latent coordinates permit a directly stated \(C^2\) Morse class and a separate finite-type hierarchy with exact uniform margins and attained worst order. Complete intervention laws add a determinant channel, while symmetric two-law quotient loss removes dependence on which competing model is declared the reference.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the synthetic product reduction, validates a genuine symmetric quotient geometry, audits the two-node Hamiltonian Morse construction environment by environment, establishes the precise radial restricted frontier, maps its strengthened rate assumptions to the retained exact-identification hypotheses, and targets the nonradial rigidity step needed for estimation and confidence sets.

body.related_work: Liang et al. establish exact CauCA recovery under almost-everywhere intervention discrepancy and exhibit determinant-one rotations on common plateaus; their exact-identification structure informs the retained intervention assumptions, while Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:identification\text{-}hypothesis\text{-}comparison}\) isolates the stronger envelopes used only for rates. Varıcı et al. derive componentwise and graph recovery from exact sparse score changes under paired node interventions; the proposed symmetric quotient modulus agrees with that qualitative conclusion at zero law error but does not claim to sharpen their theorem. Buchholz and Schölkopf use Friesecke--James--Müller rigidity to quantify near-isometric representation learning; their defect is distance from rotations rather than complete-family Hellinger error. Khesin et al. identify density space as a quotient by volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, motivating the incompressible kernel. Dacorogna--Moser and Teixeira provide prescribed-Jacobian and support-localized volume corrections. Milnor's standard definition of a nondegenerate critical point supports the directly stated \(C^2\) Morse condition. Tạ Lê Lợi and Phan Phiến provide quantitative critical-neighborhood tools under their own higher-smoothness hypotheses; those tools may inform the general finite-type analysis but are not used to justify the primary \(k=2\) class. Acartürk et al. and Lyu--Fu provide finite-sample templates for linear interventional causal representation learning and contrastive nonlinear independent component analysis. Kerkyacharian--Nickl--Picard and Bull--Nickl supply compact-manifold density concentration and confidence-set honesty machinery.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The decisive full-class upper bound is not established by the radial calculation. Symmetrizing the quotient loss removes reference-law directionality but does not prove the weighted incompressible coercivity inequality. A ratio-only strip perturbation creates a larger determinant error and therefore challenges proofs that discard the synthetic law, not the complete-law frontier. Any analytic counterexample must also integrate to two legal complete causal law families and respect the strengthened rate envelopes.
body.honest_scope: The primary class has \(n=2\), \(k=2\), \(m=1\), separated critical points, and the direct Hessian bound \(|r_i''(z)|\ge a_0\); it does not rely on a quantitative-Morse theorem that assumes higher differentiability. The general class treats \(1\le m\le k-1\) as a novel finite-type rate condition with common margin \(a_0\), at most \(J\) critical points separated by \(\Delta_0\), and an attained order-\(m\) point for every contrast. Uniform density \(C^k\), decoder \(C^k\), and bi-Lipschitz bounds are strengthened rate-class assumptions, and the explicit periodic mechanisms with nonlinear torus shears show the class is nonempty. Exact plateau rotations and almost-everywhere exact recovery remain prior art. The two-plane lower family has dimension-independent powers only because its active support is two-dimensional and \(\lambda^{n-2}(\mathbb T^{n-2})=1\); constants may depend on fixed \(n\). The radial restricted supremum and the complete two-node calculation are theorem targets. The arbitrary nonradial upper inequality is the first-class open question. Coalescing critical points, critical submanifolds, vector-valued contrast curves, and honest adaptation to unknown \(m\) remain outside the primary claim.
